title: The unit cache test isolates the path key input, so dropping u['path'] from _unit_key fails it
goal: In the unit-cache test of _tools/test_live_kb.py (ST-dvzdykit, 3678c14eb), the case for the unit's path changes only the path: it gives the new path the same title through its meta, so a _unit_key that drops u['path'] fails the test (today a changed path also changes the title, so the drop passes); the text case is isolated the same way where it can be (dropping text already fails the test's later pack step). Found by the SP-caqrexqw review.
notes: Planned at the 2026-10-10 whole-backlog triage, which the operator asked to end with every draft planned into a sprint or dropped (sprint 9 of 13, "Test suite and tools docs fixes"); it blocks no fitness test and no real user reported it, so it sits in a late sprint of the sequence. Premise: dropping u['path'] from _unit_key keeps python3 _tools/tests.py -k unit_cache green. Planned run 2026-10-10: reproduces for path; dropping u['text'] fails the test at its edited-fact pack step, so the text clause is already met and the goal is narrowed to the path case. Precheck: the tests.py -k unit_cache check passes before the work by design: it pins that the test still passes on the unmutated _unit_key. The path-case metas check is the one that fails until the work is done.
